title: RUQuant: Towards Refining Uniform Quantization for Large Language Models

problem.claim: Large language models face deployment-efficiency challenges under resource constraints.

gap.claim: Uniform quantization of weights and activations can substantially degrade accuracy because activation distributions are non-uniform.

contributions.claim: The work analyzes activation quantization using the Lloyd-Max optimality conditions and identifies how non-uniform activations shift the optimal quantization point away from the interval midpoint.

RUQuant is a two-stage orthogonal transformation method that uses blockwise composite orthogonal transformations followed by global Householder-reflection fine-tuning based on Transformer output discrepancies.
The method is reported to achieve near-optimal quantization performance without model fine-tuning in the evaluated settings.

author_reported_evidence.claim: RUQuant achieves 99.8% of full-precision accuracy with W6A6 and 97% with W4A4 quantization for a 13B LLM within approximately one minute.
A fine-tuned variant achieves higher accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large language models create deployment-efficiency challenges, and post-training quantization offers compression without retraining.
Existing uniform quantization methods can lose accuracy because activations are non-uniformly distributed.
Using Lloyd-Max conditions, the work attributes the issue to quantization points shifting away from interval midpoints under non-uniform activation distributions.
RUQuant applies blockwise orthogonal transformations and then fine-tunes a global Householder reflection using Transformer output discrepancies.
The authors report near-full-precision accuracy without model fine-tuning and higher accuracy for a fine-tuned variant.

source_observation.claim: Non-uniform activation distributions can shift the Lloyd-Max-optimal quantization point away from the interval midpoint.

interpretation.claim: Uniform quantization assumptions may introduce avoidable error when activation distributions are non-uniform.

application.claim: Quantization pipelines may benefit from distribution-aware transformations before applying uniform quantization.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this lesson generalizes across model families, tasks, or deployment settings.

unknowns: Evaluated model and task coverage beyond the stated 13B LLM is unspecified.
Benchmark datasets and comparison baselines are unspecified.
Quantization calibration and implementation details are unspecified.
The fine-tuned variant and its training procedure are unspecified.
